Working together

Know what to bring. Know what comes next.

A few practical answers before the first conversation.

Getting startedInformation & peopleOutputs & next steps

Where do we start?

+

Begin with the decision you need to make or the part of the business that needs attention. A short account of the current situation is enough for an initial conversation.

What information should we bring?

+

Relevant plans, operating information and team observations help establish the context. Bring what is available and identify where the evidence is incomplete.

Who should be involved?

+

Include a decision owner and the people closest to the question. The right group depends on the scope and how the work affects the business.

What will the work produce?

+

Define the outputs with the team at the beginning: a review, a set of priorities, a workshop record or an action plan. Connect each output with the decision it needs to support.

What if the question changes?

+

Keep the question and assumptions visible as the work progresses. Review new information together before changing the agreed direction or scope.

How do we keep the next steps useful?

+

Assign owners to the actions and choose a review point. Use the review to discuss what has changed, what the team has learned and which decision comes next.
